correctness.rationale: Two separate complete enumerators agree for all 31 histogram coefficients: the orbit-based base-eight rank filter and a recursive labeled rank-six generation, with independently implemented breadth-first subset transitions. Both enumerate all 5,362,560 rank-six maps; 2,304 half-turn-fixed maps give Burnside orbit count 670,608. A third Python BFS verifies a 36-letter reset word and excludes shorter words for the unique extremal representative. The analytic input count follows from 28*720*266. Exact code and CSV are supplied and were executed from delivery paths. This is finite exact verification, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The primary nearby public table is the 8-state fixed-cycle rank-seven, not rank-six, spectrum. Those classes are disjoint; its count 141,120 and largest threshold 49 imply none of the presented rank-six coefficients or unique maximum 36. Previously published general reset algorithms, \(n\le6\) tables, and \(n\le12\) Cerny-bound verification do not establish this exact conditional histogram. The actual source sections and claim implications were inspected. Unindexed earlier computed spectra remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed historical exhaustive spectrum or exact database could contain the coefficients; no negative search proves novelty.

The theorem is a finite classification based on executable exhaustive enumeration and does not generalize to all state counts.

value.rationale: Rank deficiency of the nonpermutation letter is a canonical automata compression parameter. The complete first adjacent rank stratum to the previously published eight-state rank-seven table supplies a benchmark for exact reset algorithms: 670,608 rotation classes, unique extremal 36-step class, sharp threshold gaps, and precisely identified nonsynchronizing half-turn-stabilized orbits. These are exact motivated invariants not determined by general Cerny bounds or the rank-seven case; no paper-sized advance is required for this natural finite benchmark.
